Subject: Integration playbook + tool-calling patterns — next steps

Hi Tim / Sarah —

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our discovery and a proposed integration playbook so we can converge on a technical approach before the deep-dive:

1) High-level architecture (proposal)
- Client -> Redwood SDK (server-side recommended) with short-lived auth tokens exchanged via customer identity service.
- Routing policy: split by latency-critical vs cost-sensitive routes (real-time UX uses low-latency variant, async/background uses batched quantized model).
- Tool/function layer: explicit "tool registry" (tool definitions + contract) hosted in your app; Redwood will call tools via signed webhooks or an SDK adapter.

2) SDK setup & Auth
- Use Redwood server SDK (Node/Python) behind your backend for sensitive actions.
- Recommended auth: customer issues short-lived session tokens (10–60m) created via KMS-backed signing; Redwood exchanges and validates signatures.
- Audit logs and request-level metadata are retained for compliance (we will show sample retention settings).

3) Tool/function calling patterns (choices we discussed)
- Synchronous single-tool call: best for quick lookups (DB fetch, product info).
- Fan-out parallel calls: recommended when multiple independent tools contribute to a single response (search + price-check + availability). Use aggregate + timeout strategy.
- Orchestrated pipeline: deterministic step-by-step calls when order matters (e.g., enrich -> rerank -> format).

4) Structured output + error handling
- We recommend a strict JSON schema for tool outputs (tools: [{name,status,result,latency_ms,error}]).
- Failure modes: per-tool retries (exponential backoff), circuit breaker per tool, and a ranked fallback strategy (cached result, stale read, or graceful degraded reply).

5) Embeddings & reranker guidance
- Retrieval pipeline: dense embeddings for semantic recall, candidate pool 100–500 depending on dimension and latency; initial lightweight scorer (dot-product) -> reranker (smaller cross-encoder model) for top-k.
- Cost/latency tradeoff: run reranker only for top 10–20 candidates when 200–300ms extra latency is allowable; otherwise rely on hybrid lexical + dense scoring.

Attachments: Redwood integration playbook (v1) and a short auth diagram — both attached.

Next steps: can you confirm the follow-ups below and whether the team prefers a server-side SDK flow? If yes, we propose a technical deep-dive with your engineers (30–45m).

Proposed owners (tentative):
- SDK integration & routing: Aditya Rao
- Tool definitions & schema: Rishi Malhotra
- Procurement / token provisioning: Lauren Bishop

Thanks — available for a sync on Thurs or Friday next week.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Tim / Sarah — quick technical notes to address the questions you raised.

Partial failures & parallel execution (practical pattern)
- Fan-out async with per-tool timeouts: issue parallel non-blocking requests, wait up to N ms (configurable per route). Collect responses that arrive within the window.
- Aggregation strategy: merge deterministic fields (e.g., availability) using priority order; append optional enrichment fields when present.
- Failure handling: mark tool entry {status: "timed_out", error: "deadline_exceeded"}. Surface partial result to user with a confidence tag (low/medium/high) and a link to retry if needed.
- Retries & idempotency: tooling should be idempotent (idempotency-key header). Use 2 retries with exponential backoff for transient 5xx errors; avoid retries for 4xx.
- Circuit breaker & bulkhead: implement per-tool circuit-breaker at the SDK adapter level to prevent cascading failures.

Structured output schema (recommended minimal)
- response = {
    query_id,
    model_version,
    tools: [
      {name, status, result, latency_ms, error_code, error_message}
    ],
    aggregated_text,
    confidence_score
  }
- This helps downstream clients decide whether to show a full answer or a partial fallback.

Embeddings -> reranker trade-offs
- Retrieval only: 60–90ms typical for dense ANN search (depending on infra).
- Add lightweight scorer: +10–40ms.
- Cross-encoder reranker (small ranker optimized on a GPU): +120–300ms depending on candidates and model size. Operate reranker only on top-K (K=10 recommended) to balance cost/latency.
- Alternative: use a distilled ranker (quantized) to reduce cost where tight latency SLOs exist.

Batching & cache considerations
- Batch embedding queries server-side (group by tenant) to amortize cost.
- Use prefix/KV-cache for repeated prompt patterns to skip model calls entirely when applicable.

Happy to bring sample code snippets in the technical sync; Aditya can share an SDK demo showing the fan-out adapter.

—Rishi
